featured_reviews.name: Shraddha Viswakarma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered from **Meraki Chinese** and had a fantastic experience with both the food and packaging. Every dish arrived hot, fresh, and neatly packed, which really added to the overall satisfaction.

**Chicken Crispy** – This was perfectly cooked with a crunchy exterior and tender chicken inside. The spice level was just right, and the seasoning had a delicious smoky depth. The crispiness was maintained despite being a delivery order — impressive!

**Chicken Manchow Soup** – Warm, flavorful, and comforting. The broth was rich and garlicky, with just the right kick of spice. It had generous chunks of chicken and crunchy fried noodles on the side which added texture — exactly how a classic Manchow soup should be.

**Chicken Burnt Garlic Rice** – Aromatic and full of flavor. The garlic wasn’t overpowering, but had that lovely toasted note that paired well with the juicy chicken bits and light soy base. A great balance of taste and texture.

**Veg Manchurian** – Soft, well-cooked veggie balls in a thick, flavorful gravy. It had a slightly tangy and spicy profile that complemented the rice really well. The flavors were rich but not oily, and the portion size was generous.

Overall, I was genuinely impressed by the consistency in taste and quality across all the dishes. Will definitely be ordering again — highly recommended for anyone craving flavorful and satisfying Indo-Chinese food! 🍜🍗🥡

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Meraki Chinese, with multiple outlets across Mumbai, including Bandra West, Lower Parel, Marol, Andheri, Malad, Sanpada, and Mira Road, has made quite an impression with its high-quality Chinese cuisine. Known for its hygiene standards and excellent packaging, it’s clear that Meraki prioritizes both food quality and customer experience.

I recently ordered from the Bandra West outlet and was thoroughly impressed by every aspect of my meal. The Chicken Lollipop was an absolute standout – perfectly cooked, crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and packed with flavor. Every bite was an explosion of taste. The seasoning was spot on, and it was without a doubt one of the best chicken lollipops I’ve ever had.

For the main course, I opted for the Chicken Triple Szechwan Rice. It was the perfect complement to the chicken lollipop, with just the right amount of spice and tang. The flavors were bold and robust, but not overwhelming, and it paired beautifully with the crispy appetizer. Even my parents, who are quite discerning when it comes to food, loved it. The combination was a win across the board!

My brother also ordered the Drums of Heaven (chicken), which not only had an impeccable presentation but was equally tasty. The crispiness of the chicken, paired with the rich flavors of the sauce, made it another highlight of the meal. We couldn't get enough of it!

We also tried the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was light, flavorful, and refreshing – the perfect drink to sip on while having a great conversation. It had the ideal balance of spice and broth, making it a delightful starter.

Overall, Meraki Chinese nailed it with both the taste and presentation of every dish. The food was not only delicious, but it was also hygienically packaged, which gave extra peace of mind. Whether you're a fan of Chinese cuisine or just looking to try something new, I highly recommend Meraki Chinese. With several locations across Mumbai, it’s easy to get your hands on their delicious food no matter where you are in the city.

Ambience & Parking: ⭐⭐⭐
Decent vibe, though the seating was a bit uncomfortable. We pre-booked our table via Zomato. Valet is available, but note that they park your car on the street. A quick shoutout to the bathrooms—very clean and hygienic!

Service: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Food & Drinks:
✅ Truffle Salmon Sushi - Absolute perfection with amazing flavor. (5/5)
✅ Egg Fried Rice - Flawless, classic taste, and good portion size. (5/5)
✅ Avocado Cream Cheese Sushi - A great, creamy option. (4/5)
✅ Chicken and Chilli Oil Dumplings - Nice flavor with a good spicy kick. (4/5)
❌ Chicken Spring Roll - Pretty average, nothing memorable. (3/5)
❌ Lemon Ice Tea & Jade Mojito - Both felt a bit uninspiring for the price. (3/5)
⭐Truffle Salmon Sushi - Easily the standout dish of the entire meal!

Pricing & Value:
Our bill was around ₹4,500 for 3 people. Given the good portion sizes and quality of the mains, it felt fair.

💡Pro Tip:
Pre-book on Zomato! They have a 25% discount running, but slots are limited.

Overall:
A solid spot with remarkably fast service and excellent sushi, though it's held back slightly by average drinks and stiff seating.

Would I Recommend It?
Depends (Definitely go if you can grab the Zomato discount and stick to their top-tier sushi).

Must Try:
Truffle Salmon Sushi, Egg Fried Rice

Skip:
Chicken Spring Roll, Jade Mojito

If you're looking for a restaurant that delivers on every front — breathtaking interiors, extraordinary food, and an experience that lingers long after the meal — look no further than PF Chang's, Khar. This place is an absolute gem, and my recent visit left me completely blown away.

The interiors are nothing short of spectacular — a seamless blend of contemporary design and rich Asian-inspired aesthetics. From the dramatic lighting and intricate décor to the beautifully curated artwork and warm, inviting tones, every corner of this restaurant is Instagram-worthy. The space feels luxurious yet comfortable, making it perfect for a romantic date night, a family celebration, or a fun outing with friends. It's the kind of place where the ambiance alone is worth the visit.

Now, let's talk about the food — because PF Chang's truly takes Asian cuisine to another level. The menu is a love letter to the flavors of Asia, and every dish we tried was an absolute revelation. The dishes were bursting with bold, authentic flavors, perfectly balanced with the right amount of spice, sweetness, and umami. The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the presentation was exquisite. From the starters to the mains, each plate was crafted with care and culinary finesse. This is Asian food at its absolute finest!

The staff were warm, professional, and genuinely passionate about making your dining experience special. The team was attentive without being intrusive, and their knowledge of the menu made ordering an enjoyable experience in itself.
Overall, PF Chang's in Khar, Mumbai is a world-class dining destination that truly lives up to its global reputation. It's not just a meal — it's an experience. If you haven't visited yet, you're seriously missing out. This is one restaurant I will be returning to again and again without hesitation.
Highly recommended — a perfect 10/10! 🥢✨

Royal China is the kind of place that makes you feel underdressed even when you are dressed well.

The ambience is classy without trying too hard, dim lighting, elegant interiors, and the sort of atmosphere where people suddenly start speaking 20 percent softer. It has that proper fine dining energy where even the water arrives looking expensive.

For lovers of authentic Chinese cuisine, Royal China offers a refined and memorable dining experience, combining elegant ambiance with thoughtfully curated flavors.

I began with their mocktails — the Jade Green Cooler and Pearl of the Orient. Both were beautifully presented and refreshingly balanced, with subtle yet distinct flavor profiles that made them perfect palate openers.

The starters truly set the tone for the meal. The Spicy Lotus Root stood out with its crisp texture and bold seasoning, delivering a satisfying crunch in every bite. The Crispy Silken Tofu with Sweet Chilli Sauce was equally impressive — delicately crisp on the outside while remaining soft and silky within, complemented by a flavorful sweet and mildly spicy glaze.

Moving on to the main course, the Burnt Chilli Garlic Noodles were rich, aromatic, and packed with deep, smoky flavors that lingered pleasantly. Paired with this were the Steamed Wontons in Spicy Sauce, which were light yet indulgent, coated in a well-balanced sauce that added just the right amount of heat without overpowering the dish.

The experience concluded on a decadent note with the Chocolate Dome dessert — a visually stunning and indulgent creation that perfectly balanced richness and sweetness, making it a delightful end to the meal.

Overall, Royal China stands out as a sophisticated destination for those seeking high-quality Chinese cuisine, where each dish is crafted with attention to detail and flavor harmony.

Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌

1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.

featured_reviews.name: Riddhiman Chanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend.

featured_reviews.name: saumya poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goh jia Ting - restaurant in bandra, had been on our list for a while, so after a show, we decided to finally give it a try. To be honest, walking into an almost empty restaurant was a little concerning. We were only the second occupied table, and the place remained virtually vacant throughout our visit. Still, we were extremely hungry and the overwhelmingly positive reviews online convinced us to stay and order.

Unfortunately, things went downhill from there.

One of the strangest parts of the evening was the service. At one point, a staff member stood directly in front of our table, watching us eat for an uncomfortably long time. It wasn’t attentive service—it felt intrusive and awkward. She only moved after we specifically requested her to. It genuinely made us uncomfortable, as though we were being monitored rather than hosted.

When I requested disposable chopsticks, the staff said they had them but then handed me what looked like a stranded stirrers and then later confessed that they don’t have disposable chopstick, then why say yes at the first place. Super careless and unprofessional.

The food was even worse. The prawn tempura roll tasted like it had been fried in old, stale oil. Instead of gyoza, we were served something that resembled chicken momos. The lobster roll was completely inedible and was left untouched after a few bites.

The cocktail we ordered, made with star fruit, was equally disappointing. It was so bad that we replaced it with a simple whisky just to avoid any more unpleasant surprises.

After struggling through the starters, we decided not to risk ordering anything else and left for another restaurant to have dinner. The entire experience felt like a complete waste of money.

What started as a restaurant we were genuinely excited to try ended up being one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in Bandra. Between the awkward service, poor food quality, disappointing drinks, and overall lacklustre experience, we left wondering how the glowing reviews online could possibly reflect what we experienced.

There are far too many great dining options in Bandra to spend your time and money here.

featured_reviews.name: John Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited GONDOLA in Bandra today with great expectations for we had heard a lot about this place.

We first ordered a 'Crispy Honey Paneer'. What arrived was 'Crispy Honey CHICKEN'. We had to return it.

I ordered a a 'Medium Rare steak' with veggies, mashed potatoes & Mushroom sauce.

I got a FLATTENED PIECE OF MEAT, 'HEAVILY OVER DONE' with FRENCH FRIES, and vegetables which were overcooked and doused in oil and Soy sauce (obviously they were made for sizzlers and the lazy COOK served them with a Steak). The Mushroom sauce was a disgrace, it was a white sauce (not Brown), hinting that there was ZERO STOCK, WINE AND OTHER INGREDIENTS USED as it should've been. It was a shameful mix of Cream and diced Mushrooms, which tasted Horribly bland (not a grain of salt in it).

I returned it, for I do not like to eat meat that is over cooked like burnt leather.

Requested the order taker to PLEASE get me a proper thick piece of MEDIUM RARE steak....I advised him to tell the 'Chef' to cook it for 3 to 5 minutes each side which will do the trick.

The waiter came back with the same bed of stir fried vegetables, but this time had a decent 1 inch thick Sirloin on it. Made me happy. But my happiness was short lived, for when I cut the meat, it turned out to be a RARE. It was just lightly seared for about 1mm on the outside and TOTALLY RAW INSIDE.

As I did not wish to be infected with Gastrointestinal disease by eating raw meat, obviously I complained to the order taker and sent back the steak for the SECOND TIME. This probably frustrated the inexperienced 'COOK' (Cannot insult the Chef's  profession by calling this person who messed up a simple steak and who has NO CLUE about sauces or even about how veggies are served with a steak, a CHEF). He just clobbered the lovely shaped sirloin with a meat tenderizer, FLATTENED IT COMPLETELY and sent it back to me within 1 minute.

I asked the order taker, what kind of 'COOK' he had, who is continously messing up a simple order. The poor order taker  who was doing a wondefdul job and was most courteous, looked visibly embarassed.

Finally, not wanting to take a chance, I accepted the ordertakers suggestion and ordered a Chicken instead. Th chicken which was obviously prepared for a sizzler as it was cooked with all the ingredients used for sizzlers. I was too tired to complain a 4th time, so quietly ate the Chicken, heavily doused in Soy sauce....

It was a horrible night, totaly ruined by a horrible cook, who truly does not belong in a classy place like GONDOLA.

I definitely will never return to GONDOLA, but if the OWNER of GONDOLA gets to read this review, he would be doing his restaurant a favour by FIRING THE HORRIBLE COOK, sobhe does not lose more customers.

Finally, please do not take your customers for granted and serve them anything you feel like to save money. Just because you serve a lot of sizzlers, it does not mean that you serve the vegetables you have pre-prwpared for sizzlers, along with all your dishes.

Reapect your clients, give them their money's worth. If you serve them garbage, like I was served today, you will ultimately not have any customers left to fool.

The service and the attitude of all the wait staff was good. I truly felt bad for the order taker, who was doing a wonderful job, but the COOK let him down with the horrible food.

What a SHAME!!!

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of bold flavors and comforting desi Chinese, Fat Kong is the kind of place that satisfies every craving with just the right hit of spice, crunch, and umami.

Crispy Chicken:
This dish was a knockout. The chicken pieces were perfectly battered—thin, golden, and fried to a shatteringly crisp texture. The outside had that addictive crunch, while the inside stayed juicy and tender. Tossed in a sticky, mildly spicy glaze with hints of garlic, soy, and chili, it was garnished with spring onions and sesame seeds, making it hard to stop at just one piece.

Chicken Triple Rice & Schezwan Noodles:
The Chicken Triple Rice was a full-on flavor bomb—a mix of fried rice and schezwan gravy poured generously on top, loaded with chopped veggies, chicken chunks, and a fried egg to top it all off. It was hearty, spicy, and soul-satisfying in that uniquely desi-Chinese way.

The Schezwan Noodles had a perfect wok-char (you know that smoky “wok hei” touch), with the right chewiness and a punchy garlic-chili flavor that didn’t overpower. Again, the chicken pieces were soft and well-seasoned, blending nicely with the heat of the schezwan sauce and the crunch of stir-fried vegetables.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It's with a heavy heart that I have to give 2 stars to a restaurant which was one of my favourites earlier on. Before the restaurant was located on SV Road Opposite Dynasty restaurant and everything was top class. It was one of those restaurants where we visited every weekend and it was always full so we had to wait 15 to 20 mins to get a table, and it was worth the wait.

So after around a decade I decided to revisit this restaurant for nostalgia and to try their iconic starters which made me drool earlier on.

So they are having two outlets now Jogeshwari and Khar, I visited the Khar outlet and was happy to see the restaurant maintaining their yellow and red colour theme. I was the only one present in their restaurant and was greeted by Akshay the person managing this outlet.

After requesting that I wish to try 2 dishes he was kind enough to give me 1/2 portion of my favourite Chicken Lollipop Hakka Style and Full portion of Crispy Spinach Chicken.

As soon as the lollipops were served the aroma transported me to the old era it was so beautiful and they have done well to maintain their taste as it was before.

But now comes the sad part, I got a piece of plastic spoon in my mouth while having the dish and was angry, disappointed and sad. I was advised by some of my friends that I should avoid the restaurant as it's not maintained the same way like before, but still I decided to try and I was like this is the end of Fatkongs for me.

I requested the Manager to not charge me for this dish and speak to the owner regarding this but he was helpless and they decided not to take away the charges.

Even though this incident took place I still ate the second dish Crispy Spinach Chicken, but it was nowhere close to the one which I used to eat before. The spinach didn't seem fresh and the chicken had a thick coating and wasn't good. So with a heavy heart I left the restaurant putting down a message to the owner who did give me a call and tried to give explanation and reasoning, though admitting that it wasn't right. But somehow I didn't feel like trying this restaurant again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited House of Mandarin, Bandra for lunch and had a pleasant experience overall, mainly because of the lovely seating arrangement and the extremely courteous staff. The ambiance truly sets the right tone.

However, the food didn’t match the expectations we had from the place.

What we tried:

Crispy Lamb Mandarin Style:
The flavours were nice and it did have a good crisp, but it turned out quite oily and a bit salty. Additionally, the lamb itself was hard to distinguish while chewing.

Crispy Prawn Cheung Fun:
This was the highlight of our meal. The prawns were extremely fresh, and the dish had a perfectly balanced taste. Definitely recommended.

Mandarin Fried Rice in Lotus Leaf (Chicken):
Expected this to be a standout, but it was fairly average and didn’t have the depth of flavour we anticipated.

Chicken Manchurian Gravy:
Unfortunately, this was too salty, making it difficult to pair with the fried rice.

Overall, it’s still a decent spot for lunch thanks to the ambience and service, but the dishes could use some refinement to match the vibe and expectations.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Yasmeen, 

Thank you for your detailed and honest review, we are glad that you liked our service and ambience. However, we are sorry to hear that the food did not meet your expectations.

Your feedback is very important to us and we have shared this with our culinary team for review, as we continue to improve. We hope that you’ll give us another opportunity to serve you a much better experience, the next time around.

Warm Regards,
Team HOM

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to House of Mandarin in Bandra, and I must say it has improved a lot since my last time. It is slightly on the expensive side compared to other Chinese restaurants, but the food quality and flavors make it worth it. The place is well suited for families for both lunch and dinner.

We started with fried corn and water chestnut starter, which turned out to be a hidden gem, perfectly crispy and full of flavor. The prawns tempura had a lighter coating this time, though I wish it had been a bit crunchier like before.

The yummy spicy crab soup lived up to its name. It was enough for two people to have plenty.

The blue pea flower fried rice with smoked chicken was the star of the meal, beautifully smoky and absolutely delicious. I wish we could have one more serving of it.

Coming to main course, glazed pork had a different flavor than I expected; I was looking for a honey-glazed sweetness, but that was my bad.

We ended the ordeal with the ice cream brownie sizzler, which was outstanding with its rich caramel sauce and perfect balance of textures.

Overall, a wonderful dining experience with delicious food and noticeable improvement since my previous visit. House of Mandarin continues to be one of the better Chinese options in Bandra.

🍱 Location: Shop No. 3/4, Mangal Bhavna, Khar Pali Rd, Khar West, Mumbai 400052
If you're a fan of sushi, dim sum, and pan-Asian cuisine, Kuai Kitchen is the place to be! The ambience here is aesthetic and welcoming, with both indoor and outdoor dining options that make it a perfect spot for a cozy meal or a catch-up with friends.
We started off with some refreshing mocktails — I tried the Martini mocktail, which was super refreshing and full of flavor. My brother went for the Panda Passion, and not only did it taste amazing, but the presentation was on point too!
Here’s what we ordered and absolutely loved:

🍣 Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll Sushi – visually stunning and tasted just as good as it looked.
🍗 Chicken with Chilli Oil and Spring Onion – bold flavors with a nice kick.

And finally, to end on a sweet note:

✨ The service was top-notch. The staff were attentive and helpful, and the manager personally guided us through the menu. Every dish was presented beautifully, and the quality was consistent throughout.
💯 Overall: 10/10 Experience
Highly recommended for all lovers of Thai, Asian, sushi, and dim sum. Add this place to your food bucket list — you won't regret it!

Cons :
1. No valet when we arrived. Had to look for parking for 15 mins.
2. Less than enthusiastic staff and thats putting lightly.
3. Small place so getting a seating inside might be difficult.
4. Lotus stem and teriyaki bao were soo sweet that it felt like eating desert. This was conveyed to the management for feedback.
5. Tatse and portion of the dishes do not justify the its cost. Too steep for the kind of mideocre food available.
6. Steamed rice was undercooked and left untouched. We had given up by this time and resorted to looking elsewhere for dinner party 2 .
7. No alcohol. Alcohol would have helped in stuffing down some of the itmes we ordered or atleast numb our taste buds enough to appreciate the food.
Pros :
1. Ambience is neat and cosy.
2. The sushi was very well made and we all enjoyed it.
3. The menu is well curated with good variety of both veg and non veg options.
I dont know if this was a one off case or our choice of items was poor or the staff was overwhelmed on a Saturday night or was it just the normal standard here but the fact remains that we were truly disappointed 😔 by the experience.

Absolutely delicious! This place serves some of the best Thai food I've ever had. Every dish was full of flavor, perfectly balanced, and made with fresh ingredients. The Pad Thai was spot on—savory, slightly sweet, and not overly oily. The special sushi the perfect kick, and the Thai iced tea was the cherry on top.

The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the service was quick. If you're craving authentic Thai cuisine with bold, vibrant taste, this is the spot. Highly recommend and definitely  gonna come again ☺️

featured_reviews.name: niveditha udyawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We ordered Chicken Katsu Curry and Raw Mango, thai cold coffee and Papaya Prawns Salad. Loved it!! The portion size was good for 2. Very filling.
The staff was very friendly and did a great job by informing us to not over order as their portion size were huge.

It's a small and well maintained place with about 14 seatings available. Neatly tucked into the lanes of Bandra.
